rulers.title: King of the Sources of the River Who Will Pacify Han

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 189-214; no Cliopatria row. 'Song Jian's group in Fuhan (in present-day Gansu)'; he 'ruled the region of Fuhan and Heguan in isolated autonomy for almost thirty years'. A 80 km circle at Linxia stands for it; Heguan is not placed on the page.

ledger.note: 189: Song Jian holds Fuhan. The rebellion 'finally splintered into three groups' in 189, 'Song Jian's group in Fuhan'; he later 'proclaimed himself to be King of the Sources of the River Who Will Pacify Han'. The page gives no year for the title, and 'almost thirty years' of rule to 214 would put the start near 185; 189 is the page's split.
214: Fuhan falls. 'Song Jian died, his capital of Fuhan was captured, and his officials were all killed by Xiahou' (Xiahou Yuan's expedition of 214).
214: Song Jian's kingdom ends with the capture of Fuhan by Xiahou Yuan.

wars.name: Xiahou Yuan's expedition against the Di and Song Jian
wars.outcome: Xiahou Yuan captured Fuhan; Song Jian died.

certainty.note: Only Fuhan and Heguan are named.

sources.title: Liang Province rebellion
sources.note: The 184-189 rebellion: Jincheng, 187 sway over the entire province, Meiyang 185, Chencang 188-189, the three groups of 189, Song Jian to 214.

notes: Song Jian, the Fuhan kingdom 189-214. 1 page used (Liang Province rebellion); the English Wikipedia 'Song Jian' is an engineer. Unsettled: the year of the royal title (page silent); 'almost thirty years' against the 189 split; Heguan's place; the extent. Counterparts: cao-cao exists; liang-province-rebels is written by this batch.
